item.title: Rainibogi to receive $15,000, Daunakamakama $5,000 for Commonwealth Games success
item.description: Commonwealth Games medal-winners Taniela Rainibogi and Jasmine Daunakamakama will receive cash rewards for their achievement at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games. Rainibogi will receive $15,000 for his gold medal achievement, while Daunakamakama will be awarded $5,000 after becoming the first Fijian woman to win a boxing medal.
item.content:encoded:
Commonwealth Games medal-winners Taniela Rainibogi and Jasmine Daunakamakama will receive cash rewards for their achievement at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games.

Rainibogi will receive $15,000 for his gold medal achievement, while Daunakamakama will be awarded $5,000 after becoming the first Fijian woman to win a boxing medal.

Minister for Youth and Sports Jese Saukuru made the announcement during the Team Fiji Thanksgiving Dinner at the Holiday Inn.

Saukuru says the Government rewards will be paid directly into the respective bank accounts of the two athletes.

item.title: Lelean to face Grammar in Super Deans U18 final
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 15/08/2026 Lelean Memorial School will meet Suva Grammar School in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans Under-18 final next Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 15/08/2026

Lelean Memorial School will meet Suva Grammar School in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans Under-18 final next Saturday.

The rain did not dampen the spirits of the boys from Davuilevu as they ran rampant against Nasinu at HFC Bank Stadium.

The first half was tight as both teams matched each other's momentum, with Lelean leading Nasinu 5-0 at half-time.

Lelean regained their composure in the second half and managed to pull away from Nasinu.

They scored another four tries in the second half to seal the win.

Meanwhile, Suva Grammar thrashed Ra High School 51-0 in their semi-final at Churchill Park in Lautoka.

In other results, QVS defeated MGM High School 22-15, while Ratu Navula College edged RKS 26-25 in the Under-14 semi-finals.

In the Under-15 semi-finals, RKS came from behind to edge rivals Queen Victoria School 28-26, while Marist Brothers High School defeated Lelean Memorial School 16-3.

In the Under-16 semi-finals, QVS beat MGM High School 17-15, while Suva Grammar thrashed Nasinu Secondary School 22-0.

In the Under-17 semi-finals, RKS defeated Methodist High School 47-29, while Suva Grammar School overcame Queen Victoria School 32-24.

In the Under-19 semi-finals, Navatu Secondary School beat RKS 22-17, while Lelean Memorial School defeated Ratu Navula College 36-27.

item.title: FTUC targets 100,000 signatures in push for $8-an-hour living wage
item.description: The Fiji Trades Union Congress is targeting 100,000 signatures in three months in support of its campaign for an $8-an-hour National Living Wage in Fiji. FTUC Assistant National Secretary Jotika Sharma says the union movement is calling on the Government to establish a National Living Wage policy, which Fiji currently does not have.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Trades Union Congress is targeting 100,000 signatures in three months in support of its campaign for an $8-an-hour National Living Wage in Fiji.

FTUC Assistant National Secretary Jotika Sharma says the union movement is calling on the Government to establish a National Living Wage policy, which Fiji currently does not have.

Speaking to fijivillage News at Terry Walk in Suva today, Sharma says the campaign follows a decision made by FTUC delegates and members at the organisation’s annual conference in Nadi in May.

She says the proposed $8 hourly rate was determined based on the union’s surveys, data and views gathered from its members.

Sharma says FTUC has launched a three-month public campaign to gather signatures from workers and members of the public, with the aim of presenting the petition to the Government around the end of October to coincide with the World Day for Decent Work.

She says the campaign aims to address rising living costs and stagnant wages while establishing clear benchmarks for determining fair wages in Fiji.

Sharma says the campaign has been taken to the public to raise awareness of the need for a National Living Wage and build broad public support.

She adds that members of the public have already shown strong support at campaign stations in Suva, Nadi and Lautoka.

Sharma says the campaign also aims to address the issue of workers leaving Fiji in search of better wages overseas.

FTUC says members of the public who cannot visit the campaign stations can also support the initiative through its online platforms.

Sharma says the union is hopeful of reaching its target of 100,000 signatures before submitting its call to the Government.

item.title: Bike Show entry was approved, we don’t condone excessive noise - Motorcyclists Association
item.description: The Fiji Motorcyclists Association has clarified concerns raised about excessive noise created by a group of motorcyclists while travelling through Laucala Beach to a recently held event. This comes after concerns were raised about excessive noise and whether bikers are allowed to ride in groups through residential areas during busy traffic periods.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Motorcyclists Association has clarified concerns raised about excessive noise created by a group of motorcyclists while travelling through Laucala Beach to a recently held event.

This comes after concerns were raised about excessive noise and whether bikers are allowed to ride in groups through residential areas during busy traffic periods.

The Association says its members were officially invited to participate in the event, with Police approval provided.

It says the motorcycle entry was part of an organised and controlled environment, with members participating in a Bike Show and promoting awareness of motorcycles and the motorcycling community.

The Association says while it is aware of comments regarding noise, to its knowledge, no official complaint was made to the Association or the event organisers regarding the particular incident.

It says it does not condone unnecessary noise pollution, excessive revving, reckless riding or disruptive behaviour on public roads.

The Association says it continues to encourage responsible riding and respect for all road users.

It also says performance motorcycles are naturally capable of producing significant engine noise, and controlled displays are part of showcasing the machines and creating awareness about motorcycles.

The Association says being seen and heard can also contribute to motorcycle safety by reminding other road users to be aware of motorcycles and to share the road responsibly.

It remains committed to promoting safe, responsible and respectful motorcycling and working with the Fiji Police Force, relevant authorities, event organisers and the wider community.

Meanwhile, Police are advising residents who have concerns about groups of bikers riding through residential areas and allegedly creating excessive noise to lodge a report.

item.title: Human Rights Commission calls for investigation into alleged assault of 16-yr-old student by teacher
item.description: The Fiji Human Rights and Anti-Discrimination Commission has raised concerns after a 16-year-old student was allegedly slapped by a teacher at Gospel High School. The student's mother, Neeshu Chand, told fijivillage News that the incident occurred last Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Human Rights and Anti-Discrimination Commission has raised concerns after a 16-year-old student was allegedly slapped by a teacher at Gospel High School.

The student's mother, Neeshu Chand, told fijivillage News that the incident occurred last Thursday.

The Commissioner Alefina Vuki says schools must be safe spaces for students and free from bullying, intimidation and all forms of violence.

It says the Constitution provides every person with the right to security and to be free from violence at home, school, work or any other place.

Vuki is calling on Police and the Ministry of Education to promptly and impartially investigate the allegation.

She says appropriate action should be taken in accordance with the law and established disciplinary procedures, while ensuring due process for everyone involved.

The Commissioner says students should also have safe and confidential access to designated child protection officers in every school and should know how and where to report violence, bullying or other behaviour that threatens their safety and wellbeing without fear of retaliation.

It also acknowledges the pressures faced by teachers, including overcrowded classrooms and growing challenges associated with illicit drugs and substance abuse among students.

Vuki further says teachers should be provided with adequate counselling, psychosocial support and practical assistance to help them manage stressful and complex classroom environments.

She stresses that every child has the right to learn in an environment where their safety, dignity and best interests are protected, adding that violence has no place in schools.

item.title: Mother who lost son to cancer says she will back party promising children's cancer hospital
item.description: Miriama Tabua, whose son Isoa Bale lost his battle with muscle cancer two years ago, participated in the WOWS Walk this morning. She says one of the issues that continues to trouble her is the level of support available for children with cancer , particularly those from low-income families without life insurance.
item.content:encoded:
Miriama Tabua, whose son Isoa Bale lost his battle with muscle cancer two years ago, participated in the WOWS Walk this morning.

She says one of the issues that continues to trouble her is the level of support available for children with cancer , particularly those from low-income families without life insurance.

Tabua says when her family learned that Isoa had an aggressive and uncommon form of cancer, they tried to find ways to send him overseas for treatment and turned to the Government for assistance.

She further says the family was told government assistance was available for children with a 100 percent survival rate, but Isoa did not qualify because of the aggressive nature of his cancer and his low chances of survival.

She adds that she does not want another parent to experience the same pain her family went through when they lost Isoa.

Meanwhile, about 100 people participated in the WOWS Walk at Albert Park this morning.
